entries.claim: The writable-open bring-forward explicitly drops legacy observation columns without describing any migration or preservation of their values, despite classifying observations as kept data that cannot be reconstructed from block rows.
entries.failure_scenario: Opening an existing format-2 store that still contains data in one of DROPPED_OBSERVATION_COLUMNS executes the drop and permanently discards those values. Because observations may outlive retention of the underlying block rows, that information cannot necessarily be regenerated.

counter_evidence.note: The artifact changes no code: git diff --stat adce27d..3adbf77 lists four files, all under docs/design/, 1030 insertions and no .rs or SQL file, so nothing in this range can drop a column. The sentence documents shipped code: fn drop_summary_columns runs ALTER TABLE observations DROP COLUMN only for the names in crates/terminus-core/src/store/schema.rs DROPPED_OBSERVATION_COLUMNS (status, model, prompt_version, topic, outcome, decisions, learned, unresolved, raw, tokens), and that constant's doc comment states they are the session-summary columns observations carried while Terminus called a model, which Store::open drops from any store that still has them. Terminus no longer calls a model, so the drop is the deliberate, already-shipped removal of those abandoned summaries, with no preservation step in the code for the doc to describe. The kept-data classification in docs/design/0004-archive-and-block-rows.md applies to the observations table's rows, which drop_summary_columns does not touch. The doc states the drop as the code performs it, so the diff introduces no schema change and misstates none.

entries.claim: The reindex operation is internally contradictory: it says every table in DERIVED_TABLES is dropped and recreated, then says evicted sessions' derived rows are left standing. Dropping the tables necessarily removes those rows.
entries.failure_scenario: A store contains an evicted session whose block rows have been deleted but whose derived rows remain searchable. If reindex follows the stated drop-and-recreate procedure, those rows are deleted and cannot be rebuilt, permanently losing the only remaining searchable representation of that session.

counter_evidence.note: The doc describes two paths and the code has two paths. fn reindex counts evicted sessions into preserved, and only when preserved == 0 does it run DROP TABLE IF EXISTS over DERIVED_TABLES in reverse. When preserved > 0 the drop loop is skipped, CREATE_SQL is a no-op on existing tables, each evicted session is skipped with continue, and each rebuilt session's rows are removed by clear_derived(&tx, &session_key) before re-derivation. The cited sentence says the rows of the sessions being rebuilt are deleted by turn id instead when the store holds an evicted session, and the word instead names the second path as the replacement for the drop. Nothing in the diff says both happen on one store, so there is no contradiction and no path on which evicted rows are dropped.
